judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade 3 (rank 3) Skill bullets under the same Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading sub-strand, the first in Term 1 ('Uses phonics, contextual and structural analysis decoding skills when reading both silently and aloud') and the second in Term 2 ('Uses phonics, context clues and structural analysis decoding skills when reading unfamiliar words'). The two bullets name the same decoding repertoire (phonics, context, structural analysis) and differ only in the reading situation named; 'contextual analysis' and 'context clues' are the same strategy in different wording. The bounded evidence shows no substantive extension - no longer or harder texts, no increased independence, no broader letter/word scope, no added skill component - so a Term 1 to Term 2 developmental claim is not supported even though that direction would be permitted. The pairing is nevertheless more than generic repetition: it is the deliberate CAPS reinforcement of one decoding toolkit applied in complementary contexts (silent and oral reading of connected text, and attack on unfamiliar words) within the same sub-strand, which is genuine instructional coherence without dependency. Hence symmetric relatesTo in canonical endpoint order with null direction. Evidence limitation: 24 source-evidence items are omitted for each endpoint and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the supplied statement text, identity scopes and LC metadata.

Within the same grade, direction may only run from the earlier to the later term, so the only admissible developmental direction is second_to_first. The change is substantive rather than mere repetition: Term 1 oral answering is anchored to a heard story and largely recall-level, whereas Term 2 broadens the question types to include open-ended questions and adds justification ('gives reasons for answers'), so competence in answering story-based listening questions plausibly supports success with the more demanding open-ended, reason-giving oral responses. Shared Grade ancestor and token overlap alone were not treated as sufficient; the term order plus the expansion in question type and required justification carry the judgment. Both endpoints have truncated source evidence and upstream merge/audit context on endpoints and ancestors, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: First SFI is Grade 1 / Term 1 / Reading and Phonics / Emergent reading skills: 'Develops basic concepts of print' (concept of book; concept of text - word, same words, letter, names of letters, one-to-one correspondence; directionality of reading; punctuation including capital letter and lowercase letter). Second SFI is Grade 1 / Term 4 / Writing / Handwriting: 'Forms lower and upper case letters correctly and fluently according to size and position, that is, starts and ends in the correct place'. There is genuine, pair-specific conceptual coherence: recognising letters, letter names and the capital/lowercase distinction, together with left-to-right print orientation, is complementary to producing upper and lower case letter forms in handwriting. However, the second statement is not a substantive extension, deepening or combination of the first: it is a distinct motor-production competence in a different Skill Area and Sub-strand (Writing / Handwriting), developed through its own strand across the year, so proficiency in the print-concepts bullet does not in itself underwrite success in fluent letter formation. The strongest nomination signals are lexical and trigram overlap ('letters', 'position', 'starts', 'ends') whose referents differ across the two statements (front/back of a book and position on a page versus stroke start/end points and letter size on the writing line), which cannot establish developmental dependency. Canonical relatesTo (symmetric, null direction) is therefore the correct complete judgment rather than buildsTowards or no_relation. Limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and all endpoint and ancestor SFIs carry upstream audit/merge context, so this rests on the bounded excerpts supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3) Skills but sit in different strands: the first is Term 1 Listening and Speaking (Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities) — 'Asks questions for clarification and comments on what was heard'; the second is Term 2 Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading — 'Answers a range of higher order questions based on the passage read'. Their shared substance is comprehension-through-questioning: oral clarification questions and commenting on heard text reinforce the same interpretive engagement required when responding to higher order questions about a read passage (LC tags 'questions/listening/clarification' vs 'comprehension/higher order questions/shared reading'). However, the acts differ materially (generating clarifying questions and comments about oral input vs answering interpretive questions about a written passage) and no evidence shows the oral skill as support for success in the reading-comprehension skill, so a developmental Term 1 to Term 2 buildsTowards is not warranted; the overlap signals (shared token 'questions', shared Grade ancestor, weak rank proximity) are too generic to assert dependency. Coherent complementary comprehension skills, hence a symmetric relation. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream merge/audit context, so the judgment rests only on the bounded excerpts supplied.

Since same-grade, same-term coordinates cannot supply direction and same-rank buildsTowards requires substantive extension evidence, canonical symmetric relatesTo is the correct judgment. Nomination signals are weak (grade rank_gap 0 'weak', page_gap 0 'weak', one shared token 'words', one shared LC tag 'phonics') and do not establish development. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Term 2, Skill Area EMERGENT WRITING, but under different printed sub-strands: 'Role plays writing in play situations: makes greeting cards, writes letters etc.' (Sub-strand 'Emergent Writing:') and 'Copies patterns onto pegboards and copies patterns, words and letters onto paper' (Sub-strand 'Handwriting'). They are substantively coherent complementary facets of emergent writing - purposeful pretend/role-play writing for real communicative purposes alongside fine-motor copying of patterns, words and letters - and LC evidence confirms the copying skill is handwriting/fine-motor focused ('copying', 'handwriting', 'patterns', 'pegboards') while the role-play skill is tagged 'role play', 'play situations'. The nomination's lexical overlap ('letters') is a false friend: in the first statement 'letters' means correspondence/greeting cards, in the second it means alphabetic letters, so it supports no developmental claim. Same grade and same term, with no source evidence that either capability is a condition for or an expansion of the other, so a directional buildsTowards is unwarranted; symmetric relatesTo fits. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting further pair-specific detail.

judgment.rationale: Both are distinct printed bullets in the same Grade 1 / Term 3 / Listening and Speaking (Oral) / 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' sub-strand (same rank, Grade 1; no term difference available to order them). Their content is substantively coherent beyond shared wording: 'Sequences pictures of a story and matches captions with the pictures' works with story pictures and existing captions, while 'Listens to a story with interest and enjoyment, drawing a picture and writing a caption about it' has learners produce a picture and caption in response to a heard story (LCs: sequencing pictures of a story / matching captions with pictures vs listening to a story, drawing a picture, writing a caption). These are complementary receptive-reconstructive and productive responses to story listening that reinforce the same picture-caption-story link. The evidence does not show one as substantively more complex or as a condition for the other within the same term, so a developmental direction is not supported; symmetric relatesTo is the defensible judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, which bounds but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade 2 (rank 2), the first under Term 1 / Writing / Handwriting ('Writes and uses punctuation marks (full stops, question marks, commas, exclamation marks)') and the second under Term 4 / Listening and Speaking / Daily-Weekly activities ('Uses terms such as noun, adjective, verb, pronoun, preposition, comma, question mark, paragraph when talking about own writing'). The direction Term 1 to Term 4 within the same grade is valid. Substantively, practical competence in writing and correctly using punctuation marks (including commas and question marks, explicit in the Term 1 LCs 'Writes punctuation marks...' and 'Uses punctuation marks...') supports the later, more abstract metalanguage demand of naming and discussing those same features ('comma', 'question mark') when talking about one's own writing; the Term 4 statement additionally extends into grammatical terminology and oral reflection, so it is a broadening and deepening rather than mere repeated wording. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), and the shared-token nomination signals alone are weak, so this judgment rests on the printed statement texts, Term/Skill Area scopes and LC tags supplied.

The first describes applying phonics, contextual and structural analysis decoding plus comprehension skills to make meaning; the second describes the guided-reading routine of reading silently and aloud from own book at the group's instructional level. judgment.rationale: Both Skills resolve to Grade 3 (rank 3) / Term 2 / Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading with the same identity_scope_key and the same direct parent Sub-strand, and both are printed bullets in the same table body cell (row=3, window 46, page 117). The first SFI is an analytic shared-reading move - using visual cues to identify an advertisement's purpose and intended audience - while the second is the whole-class shared-reading practice of reading enlarged texts (poems, big books, posters, electronic texts) with the teacher. They are complementary practices on overlapping visual/enlarged text types within one shared-reading block, giving genuine pair-specific instructional coherence beyond generic repetition, so relatesTo is warranted. buildsTowards is not supported: within the same Grade and the same Term the evidence shows no substantive extension, increased independence, broader text range or dependency - only identical hierarchy, zero rank gap, zero page gap and trivial token overlap ('and', 'the', 'reading'), none of which alone establish developmental direction. Evidence limits: both endpoints have 24 omitted source-evidence items and carry upstream audit/merge context, so the bounded excerpt may not reveal all sequencing information.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0) EMERGENT WRITING. The second SFI is Term 1, Sub-strand 'Emergent Handwriting' ('Develops fine-motor control to strengthen fingers: plays finger rhymes ... rolls small paper balls between fingers'); the first SFI is Term 2, Sub-strand 'Emergent Writing' ('Understands that writing and drawing are different and begins to copy letters and numerals ... pretend writing using a mixture of copied letters and squiggles'). Direction is Term 1 to Term 2 within the same grade, which is permitted. Finger strength and fine-motor control developed in Term 1 are the physical control that makes purposeful mark-making, copying of letters and numerals from the classroom environment, and sustained pretend writing more likely to succeed in Term 2; the Term 2 statement adds a conceptual distinction (writing vs drawing) and a concrete copying task rather than merely repeating the Term 1 wording, so this is substantive extension, not generic repetition. The nomination's lexical signals (shared token 'to', shared LC tag 'emergent') are weak and were not relied on. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the judgment rests on the printed statement text, identity scope (grade/term/skill area/sub-strand) and LCs supplied.
